perspective:
Arthur’s available information:

- He knows he is Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate, and knows Teresa Ortega as a medical assistant/professional colleague. They collaborate on community service projects.
- During the project, Arthur observed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed.
- Arthur asked if he could help. Teresa said it was kind but she thought she could manage because there was a lot to do.
- Arthur told her self-care mattered and offered help. Teresa accepted help organizing medical supplies. They began working.
- Arthur believed Teresa was hesitant because she wanted to prove her capability. He felt empathetic and told her accepting help does not mean she is incapable. Teresa said she appreciated it and wanted to show she could do it herself. Arthur said teamwork can be more effective. Teresa said she sometimes needs reminding of that.
- Later, Arthur believed Teresa was still struggling. He felt frustrated that his help was not yielding results and wanted another way to support her. He told her he could see things were still tough and that she was doing a great job. Teresa said it had been a busy day and she felt behind. Arthur suggested working together; Teresa agreed.
- Arthur felt hopeful about the collaborative approach. He told Teresa so. Teresa said it already felt less overwhelming. Arthur proposed he handle inventory while Teresa managed patient records, with regular check-ins. Teresa agreed. Arthur felt glad.
- Arthur believed their teamwork strengthened their professional relationship and felt satisfied. He told Teresa their teamwork had paid off; Teresa agreed. He suggested continuing the collaborative approach in future projects; Teresa agreed and thanked him. Arthur looked forward to their next project together.
- Arthur does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts or unspoken feelings beyond what she said or what he inferred from her behavior.
